title: Immutable Generated Snapshot And Request Admission
summary: P2 Core foundation separates owned immutable artifact bytes from publication locks and per-request source freshness; retrieval algorithms remain shared with the CLI.

buildInterface.embed: Set SHIN_CONTEXT_BUILD_CLI=OFF before adding this source tree as a CMake subdirectory; link the caller to shin-context-core. HTTP, PostgreSQL and Server policy are not Core dependencies.
api: execute_agent_context_pack with the same admitted session

scope: CLI/in-memory search, context, Brief and Pack parity
serverIntegration: Authorized search/Brief/Pack routes and bounded global residency are described in shin-server-retrieval-v1. The earlier native-foundation benchmark remains historical dev.2 evidence, not HTTP capacity.

ownership.snapshot: GeneratedSnapshot owns verified manifest and immutable artifact bytes in a private unlinked file mapping, plus the selected root/output/profile route. Streaming capture verifies the existing hashes before mapping; source truncation or replacement cannot mutate the retained inode. It owns no IndexLock, thread, source files, freshness claim or lazy mutable query cache.
ownership.request: RetrievalSession owns request admission metadata and a shared immutable generation. Each GeneratedInput has its own cursor. Concurrent requests never seek one shared stream.
ownership.cli: Short-lived CLI sessions may retain their existing reader lock and read filesystem artifacts. The same row decoders, candidate discovery, ranking, evidence projection and Pack selection operate on both backings.
ownership.server: Server owns route authorization, active-generation choice, aggregate resident budgets and eviction. A Core per-generation load cap is not a server-wide cache or RSS cap.

load.locking: Hold an existing shared publication lock only while verifying and capturing one complete generation. Release it before returning the immutable owner.
load.validation: Require matching profile id/config fingerprint and generator, exact manifest/output integrity and safe generated layout. Validate byte budgets before hashing each artifact, then hash the captured bytes against the same manifest.
load.memoryAccounting: Payload bytes count manifest and stored artifact text, not resident RAM. The private backing inode consumes temporary disk space until its last mapping closes, including process termination. Read-only mapped pages are faulted on demand. C++ metadata, temporary buffers and request allocations are additional; RSS and macOS physical footprint are measured separately.
load.format: Generator identity is unchanged because this is an in-process representation, not a new persisted index format or compatibility reader.

freshness.snapshotOnly: A loaded-session constructor with require_current=false reports verified-generated-snapshot, not-assessed source freshness and the captured snapshot id. It can continue reading historical bytes after publication changes or artifact removal.
freshness.requireCurrent: Acquire a short shared publication lock, perform the existing exact-current assessment and require its manifest id to equal the captured generation. Release the lock before retrieval. A changed active generation is rejected; the caller must explicitly select and admit a new generation.
freshness.continuityEvaluation: Core dev13 adds the existing verified_snapshot/verified_current open modes for a resident RetrievalSession. These modes retain the shared lock for one bounded checkpoint/resume/Impact evaluation that compares source and publication. They do not change the original bool constructor or give the long-lived GeneratedSnapshot a lock. The native evaluator rejects an inconsistent supplied root/output/profile binding.
freshness.observationBoundary: Freshness is assessed at request admission, not a promise that external files cannot change afterward. RAM residency never prolongs the proof. A later request must assess again.
freshness.noFallback: A missing artifact in a loaded view is an error, never permission to read that artifact from the current filesystem publication or mix generations.
freshness.noSideEffects: Admission and query do not rebuild, repair, publish, adopt, execute commands or mutate source.

required: Publication completes while an old loaded session remains alive
Old and new generations remain distinct
Retrieval survives removal of generated files after load
Current admission detects source drift and changed publication
